correctness.rationale: The unique binary tiling 1(1|00)* gives F_L length-L members. For every nonmaximal word, replacing its final 00 tile and the trailing ones by the minimal compatible tail computes its unique immediate successor, giving Δ_t. There are F_{L-t-2} prefixes; Fibonacci summation exhausts all F_L−1 internal gaps. Explicit inter-layer boundaries yield gaps 1/2. Summing across layers and taking Fibonacci ratios gives the complete dyadic geometric frequency law. Self-contained checker independently compared all layers 1..20 and direct indicator enumeration.

originality.rationale: S itself and its tiling definition are previously known, particularly OEIS A060142/A086747. The claimed complete adjacent-gap spectrum, exact layerwise multiplicities, and dyadic limit were not identified in full examined matching records or available semantic published-result summaries; alternate-name implication and historical-priority limitations are explicitly retained. This is qualified same-model originality, not an independent certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed first-difference characterization under odd-composition or automatic-word aliases may establish the same formulas.
The 1976 article was accessible bibliographically but its entire full text was not inspected; no claim of full-text negative coverage is made.
A source documenting exact successor formulas (rather than just the sequence itself) could cover this result implicitly.

value.rationale: The number-theoretically natural return gap between successive one positions of the classical Baum–Sweet automatic word is determined completely, not just as a sample table. Exact Fibonacci counts at every dyadic level and a nondegenerate limit reveal a structural distribution and exponential lacunarity of allowed large gaps. These are useful for recurrence and sampling questions and are not a mere restatement of membership or an arbitrary slice.
